doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Diana Krall studying with Jimmy Rowles
summary: Hanna played behind Krall and warned her about studying in Canada; Rowles a genius.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: working with her. But they don’t have any drums, they just have a bass — Nat Cole voicings you know, uh, instrumentation, not voicing. And she was going to study, she was studying with Jimmy Rowles . And I played with them one night. Her mother and father said, “Will you play with them, play behind my daughter some night?” I said, “Sure, okay.” So we played Donte’s and she was very thankful. I says, “What are you going to do now?” She says, “Oh I’m going to Canada and study with Don Thompson.” I said, “Aren’t you studying with Jimmy Rowles?” She says, “Yeah, but then I got a scholarship to study with this guy.” “You know what that’s going to be like, honey?” She says, “Well no I hear he’s good.” I says, “It’s going to be like stepping off the top of the Empire State Building.” And I saw her about two years later and I asked her, “How you doing, how did you make out in Canada?” She says, “Oh it was very thrilling, it was just like jumping off the top of —” She never forgot that line. She’s a funny gal. “Stepping off the top—” She says no you were right, Jimmy Rowles is where I should have stayed. I said, “Well right, this guy’s a genius.” A genius Jimmy Rowles . Crazy as the day is long. Very funny man, very funny guy. Very funny fellow.
